modules.name: cli
modules.responsibility: Parse argv into structured commands, delegate to TodoService via injected dependency, format output via TodoFormatter protocol, handle errors uniformly via execute_command helper
interfaces: Protocol TodoFormatter: format_todo(todo: Todo) -> str; format_todo_list(todos: list[Todo]) -> str

modules.name: service
modules.responsibility: Business logic for todo CRUD operations, validation, and state transitions
interfaces: Protocol TodoService: add(title: str) -> Todo; complete(todo_id: str) -> Todo; remove(todo_id: str) -> None; list_todos() -> list[Todo]

modules.name: repository
modules.responsibility: Persistence of todos to JSON file, load/save lifecycle management, file permission enforcement
interfaces: Protocol TodoRepository: save(todos: list[Todo]) -> None; load() -> list[Todo]; find_by_id(todo_id: str) -> Optional[Todo]

modules.name: config
modules.responsibility: Application configuration including storage path resolution and environment-aware defaults

fields.name: id
fields.description: First 8 chars of UUID4 — typeable by user

fields.name: id_full
fields.description: Full UUID4 stored internally for uniqueness

ux_flows.name: add
steps: CLI parses title from positional arg
Service validates title non-empty, creates Todo with uuid4 and timestamp
Repository loads existing list, appends, saves
ux_flows.success_criteria: Todo appears in subsequent list output with new short ID, exit code 0
error_states: Empty title → validation error message, exit code 1

ux_flows.name: complete
steps: Service resolves short ID to full UUID, sets completed=True
ux_flows.success_criteria: Todo shows as completed in list, exit code 0
error_states: Already completed → idempotent success, exit code 0

ux_flows.name: remove
ux_flows.success_criteria: Todo absent from subsequent list output, exit code 0

ux_flows.name: list
steps: Service returns todos sorted: incomplete first by created_at, completed last
CLI formats each line: [x] id title or [ ] id title
ux_flows.success_criteria: All todos displayed with status, short ID, and title. Empty state shows 'No todos yet.'
error_states: Corrupt file → clear error with recovery hint, exit code 2

customer_journey: User installs the CLI. On first run of any command, the storage file is created automatically at ~/.todos.json with no configuration required. They run `todo add 'task'` to create their first item, `todo list` to see all items with short IDs, `todo complete <id>` when done, and `todo remove <id>` to clean up. Every operation completes in a single command with clear confirmation output. The experience requires zero setup and zero mental model beyond the four commands.

experience_metric.name: All CRUD ops in ≤1 command
experience_metric.definition: Every CRUD operation (create, read, update, delete) completes in a single CLI invocation with no prerequisite setup or follow-up command
experience_metric.target: 100% of operations: ≤1 command, ≤500ms wall time, human-readable confirmation on stdout
experience_metric.measurement: Automated: time each command in benchmark harness. Manual: UX agent verifies each flow step count.

architecture_decisions.title: JSON file persistence over SQLite
architecture_decisions.context: Trivial CLI benchmark project. Persistence must require zero setup. No concurrent writers.
architecture_decisions.decision: Store todos as a JSON array in ~/.todos.json (path overridable via TODOS_PATH env var, exposed through Config).
architecture_decisions.rationale: No database setup, no migrations, file is human-readable. SQLite would be over-engineered for a personal todo list with no concurrency requirement.
consequences: File grows unbounded — acceptable for personal use

architecture_decisions.title: Protocol-based dependency injection at all module boundaries
architecture_decisions.context: Build agent friction report: direct imports between modules made unit tests require filesystem patching (testability friction). Design revision triggered.
architecture_decisions.decision: Every cross-module dependency is declared as a typing.Protocol and injected at construction time. Wiring happens only in cli/main.py.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Resolves testability friction. Satisfies SOLID Dependency Inversion. Each module testable in isolation with a fake. No monkeypatching needed in tests.
consequences: Interface contracts are explicit and enforced by mypy

architecture_decisions.title: Short ID: first 8 characters of UUID4
architecture_decisions.context: Full UUIDs are unwieldy for CLI users to type. Experience metric requires operations in ≤1 command; long IDs degrade UX.
architecture_decisions.decision: Display and accept the first 8 hexadecimal characters of the internal UUID4 as the user-facing ID. Full UUID stored internally.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Collision probability for a personal list is negligible (birthday problem: >50% collision requires ~77,000 items at 8 hex chars). UX metric demands typeable IDs.
consequences: Theoretical collision risk irrelevant at personal-list scale
Simpler UX — IDs fit on one line without wrapping
find_by_id must scan full list for prefix match

threat_model.description: User or malicious process modifies ~/.todos.json directly, injecting malformed or oversized data
threat_model.mitigation: Validate JSON schema on load using Pydantic; malformed file yields clear error message and non-zero exit, not a crash or silent data loss

threat_model.description: Todo file readable by other users on a shared POSIX system
threat_model.mitigation: Create file with mode 0600 on first write; never log todo titles

privacy_inventory.purpose: User task tracking — content chosen and owned by the user
privacy_inventory.retention: Until explicitly removed via `todo remove` or manual file deletion
privacy_inventory.encryption: None — local file, mode 0600, single-user system
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: `todo remove <id>` for individual items; delete ~/.todos.json for full erasure

i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Not applicable — plain text CLI output has no layout engine
i18n_plan.hebrew_specifics: Not applicable for this benchmark project

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Four modules with Protocol boundaries: cli (presentation, formats output), service (business logic, validation), repository (JSON persistence, file permissions), config (path and env config). All cross-module dependencies are injected via Protocols. Wiring in cli/main.py only.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: Single entity: Todo. Fields: id (8-char UUID4 prefix, user-facing), id_full (full UUID4, internal), title (str), completed (bool), created_at (ISO 8601). Stored as JSON array. Privacy: internal, file mode 0600.

sections.title: UX Flows
sections.content: Four flows: add (1 command, confirm output), complete (1 command, idempotent), remove (1 command, confirm), list (1 command, empty-state handled). Experience metric: all ops in ≤1 command.

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001: JSON file over SQLite (zero setup). ADR-002: Protocol-based DI (resolves testability friction). ADR-003: 8-char UUID4 short IDs (typeable, collision-safe at personal scale).

sections.title: Threat Model
sections.content: Tampering via direct file edit: mitigated by Pydantic schema validation on load. Information disclosure on shared systems: mitigated by file mode 0600.

sections.title: Privacy Inventory
sections.content: Todo titles: internal classification, user-controlled content, stored locally at ~/.todos.json (0600), erasable via remove command or file deletion.
